system.name: OmniBench
system.one_liner: A self-generating, graph-based benchmark for virtual agents with five task-complexity dimensions, bottom-up task synthesis and ten evaluated capabilities.

content.variant_note: a banner of four adjectives, four colour-framed quadrants (one proof each) matched to them by underline colour, and a central capability wheel overlapping their inner corners
content.argues: OmniBench is systematic, effective, scalable and multidimensional: controlled complexity, high-quality graph data, ten evaluated capabilities, and automatic cross-platform task synthesis.
content.subject: Poster-like overview of the OmniBench benchmark: complexity grid, example task graph, evaluation charts, construction flow and the capability wheel.

encoding.line_style_means: thick coloured frames = the four claims; dotted rounded boxes = sub-parts; dashed vertical lines = column separators; dashed vertical line in the bar chart = human baseline; dashed green box on one wedge = the capability the radar profile is tied to
encoding.shape_means: wedge = capability (outer ring) or category (inner ring); pill row = difficulty level; circle node = subtask; radar polygon = a profile over axes
encoding.marker_means: Level 1-3 and Easy, Medium, Hard name the rows; letters A-G name subtasks; 1. and 2. order the construction steps; numbers on the wheel are per-capability counts; Edges, Width, Nodes, Apps, Depth captions give the measured complexity of each snippet
encoding.emphasis: the banner words are colour-linked to the quadrants, the OmniBench logo and wordmark are the largest items, and the wheel sits in the middle overlapping all four quadrants as the hub

lessons.what_to_learn: Open a benchmark figure with a banner of the paper's key adjectives, each underlined in the colour of the quadrant that proves it, and place four colour-framed quadrants around a central wheel of the capabilities; each quadrant then shows one proof (complexity grid, example record, result charts, construction flow).
lessons.suits: Benchmark or dataset papers that must show design, data quality, evaluation and scale claims in a single self-contained overview.

evidence: Overview of OmniBench, a systematic benchmark with five-dimensional task complexity and bottom-up automatic task synthesis for generating structured task graphs.
It evaluates ten virtual agent capabilities using high-quality graph-based data
we propose 10 fine-grained capabilities, derived from five categories that we consider essential

summary: OmniBench is a graph-based benchmark for virtual agents whose tasks are synthesised bottom-up with controllable complexity and evaluated on ten capabilities. Figure 1 is a poster-like composite. A banner with the OmniBench logo carries four adjectives, each underlined in the colour of one framed quadrant. Green: a grid of small task graphs for five complexity dimensions at three levels, plus a complexity radar. Red: one example task graph with its subtasks, instruction, intent and trajectories, and a bar chart showing that training on graph data helps. Blue: coverage-rate bars and a radar for open-source, closed-source and GUI agents against a human baseline of 80.1. Yellow: the automated subtask and task synthesis flow, 20 scenario groups and three platforms. A central two-ring wheel lists five categories and ten capabilities.
summary_zh: OmniBench 是按图结构自底向上合成任务的虚拟智能体基准。图 1 像一张海报：顶部标志加四个形容词，下方四个彩色方框展示五维复杂度网格、任务图样例与训练收益、十项能力的柱图和雷达图、自动构建流程与二十个场景，中央圆环列出五类十项能力。
notes: Prior kinds kept (contribution-mosaic, scope-overview, stage-pipeline) with the variant set to bento-highlights, since the prior's benchmark-dashboard is a scope-overview variant. The wheel numbers are not explained by the caption or the digest, so they are recorded as counts of unstated meaning. Two of the radar axis abbreviations are hard to read in the preview and are not spelled out. Which pictures are bitmaps is inferred from the digest (65 placed bitmaps, the wheel matches a 152 by 157 pt one); the charts may be bitmaps or vector. Icon counts are rough, read off the picture.
